title: Meeting King Oliver; why Armstrong swung more
summary: Tate introduces himself to Oliver, who knew Holder, and explains why he preferred Armstrong.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah, I met him. Oh, sure, I always made my business to introduce myself to these cats, man. Other people would want to and a lot of times they'd be a little shy, you know. Man, I'd go up and meet him. Sure, I met him and talked to him. I asked him about -- he knew Holder. He knew T. Holder. And Holder was -- would be about his age, see.
How did you feel about him? How did the musicians and all you guys feel about somebody like Oliver? Was he highly respected or was he --
Oh, no, no, no, no, no, no. He was highly respected. I just didn't like him as good as I did Louie.

But everybody else -- he was kicking their behinds, you know, and everything else. But to me, he just didn't swing as much as Louie. You understand what I mean? Louie was -- Louie started -- actually, I think Louie started swinging. Louie started (HUMMING), you know, that kind of stuff, and like it's hard to explain, but King Oliver didn't gut like Louie. He just didn't swing as much as Louie.
